nodes.heading: INTRODUCTION
nodes.own_text:
This manual was prepared after thorough examination of available and accessible
policies and procedures. An extensive and thoroughly search was done in preparation
for this manual, which resulted in a comprehensive list of policies considered to be
applicable to the Global health Development| Eastern Mediterranean Public Health
Network (GHD|EMPHNET). MAUS Business Systems was used in drafting some of
the policies and procedures included in this manual. GHD|EMPHNET is responsible
for the results of the actions taken in accordance with the information provided in this
manual.

nodes.heading: Purpose of the Manual
nodes.own_text:
The Human Resources Policies and Procedures Manual (HR PPM) is a tool that was
created to facilitate the implementation of HR and personnel related systems and
functions. This PPM defines the primary HR related policies, rules and procedures
designed for, and adopted by, GHD|EMPHNET. Additionally, it defines the necessary
steps to be followed by the Human Resources Department and other concerned
parties for particular situations and also serves in identifying responsibilities, methods,
and means of executing each step-in terms of communication channels, forms and
documents.
GHD|EMPHNET is responsible for the results of the actions taken in accordance with
the information provided in this manual. GHD|EMPHNET is committed to providing
employees with working conditions that comply with Social Security regulations and
the Jordanian Labor Law and its amendments. All GHD|EMPHNET employees work
under the conditions contained in GHD|EMPHNET’s enterprise agreement, which is
registered with the Ministry of Labor and covers all standard working conditions. In
addition, GHD|EMPHNET is committed to paying the minimum wage endorsed by the
Ministry of Labor. In the event of a conflict between the Labor law and this manual, the
Labor Law prevails.

nodes.heading: Manual Overview
nodes.own_text:
The HR Policies and Procedures Manual encompasses a number of primary human
resources functions and procedures presented through policies and standard
operating procedures, defining responsibilities, and the forms used to organize and
document the process of implementation. The topics covered in GHD|EMPHENT HR
PPM includes the following:
1- Recruitment & Selection
2- Performance Appraisal
3- Employment Contract
4- Training & Development
5- Attendance, Leaves & Vacations

6- Discipline & Grievance
7- Personnel Management

nodes.heading: 1.1 Purpose
nodes.own_text:
The purpose of Recruitment and Selection system is to provide a framework and core
principles for recruitment and selection, in line with relevant legislation and equal
opportunities best practice, to ensure that the most suitable person is appointed and
merit-based selection is accomplished and different job requirements and objectives
are met.
In this context, GHD|EMPHNET embrace the following:
The System is based on an approach that customizes the R&S process as per
the requirements of the different Managerial Levels which were identified in
the job description cards.

The System favors and supports Internal Recruitment as a tool that facilitates
the attainment of optimal utilization of GHD|EMPHNET’s current human
capital, as well as increasing retentions rate.
The R&S System is mainly handled by the HR Department, which bears the
following advantages:
Avoiding duplication of work and propagation of costs, since the HR
Department has a full oversight on the entire process.
Increased effectiveness of the R&S process, especially as the process
matures in GHD|EMPHNET, since most teams have considerable yet
similar manpower requirements; it is advantageous to have the
recruitment process mainly handled by one designated entity.
Enabling internal recruitment and thus an effective reallocation of
manpower.

nodes.heading: 1.2 Scope
nodes.own_text:
The Recruitment and Selection system is applicable to all vacant positions at
GHD|EMPHNET. Commencing from the development of the Human Resources Plan
and requesting to fill a vacancy until the end of the probationary period and converting
the employee to regular at-will employment status.

nodes.heading: 1.3 Responsibilities
nodes.own_text:
It is the responsibility of the HR Team in cooperation with all GHD|EMPHNET
departments to set and develop a Human Resources Plan.
It is the responsibility of the HR Team, concerned Directors and Team Leaders
to conduct applicant’s assessment to select and hire Full Time Employee to fill
a specific vacancy.
It is the responsibility of the HR Manager in cooperation with all
GHD|EMPHNET’s concerned Directors to fill any vacancy at GHD|EMPHNET
by identifying, attracting, screening, and shortlisting the most suitable
candidates for a specific vacancy.
It is the responsibility of the Task Owner and Human Resources Team to
oversee the recruitment and hiring of Consultants/ Contractors
It is the responsibility of the HR to ensure that all involved staff adhere to the
policies procedures related to New Employee Orientation, where the HR leads
the orientation process, and engages the new employee, the new employee's
direct manager, and other staff as needed.
It is the responsibility of the Human Resources to initiate the process of the 3-
month evaluation, based on the employee start date. The employee’s Direct
Manager, Team Leader/Director must adhere to the SOP and ensure timely
completion of the 3-month evaluation.
It is the responsibility of the Executive Director to give final approval of the
transfer of an employee between divisions, and the concerned Directors’

responsibility to approve employee’s Transfer within the same division. It is the
responsibility of all the Directors/Team Leaders/Direct Managers to point out
transfer necessity cases or assist in recommending the suitable employee. As
well as it is HR responsibility to coordinate and document all transfers.

nodes.heading: 1.4 Policies
nodes.own_text:
1. GHD|EMPHNET strives to ensure recruiting the right people, in the right place at
the right time. GHD|EMPHNET recruitment and selection system aims to ensure
attracting and appointing applicants with the right skills, knowledge, behaviors and
experience to meet the needs of all our vacancies. In light of this we ensure that
we appoint on the basis of merit and without discrimination
2. GHD|EMPHNET represented by the HR Department, is committed to ensure that
all Candidates are given equal access to information about the job vacancy and
its requirements, Candidates are considered on merit, Interviews and the selection
process are applied equally and consistently to candidates, and Selection
methods are reliable and free from bias or discrimination.
3. GHD|EMPHNET is an equal opportunity employer adopting Merit Principle to
appoint the most qualified and competent candidates, and thus:
 The attraction of qualified candidates should be a priority, utilizing various
means and the most suitable sources
 Candidates recommended by the concerned team shall be subjected to all
required process checks, where all candidates shall be treated equally
regardless of the source of recommendation
 The selection shall be based on a thorough assessment of the required
competencies
 No candidate shall pass to the next phase throughout the recruitment and
selection process unless meeting the minimum requirements of each phase
4. GHD|EMPHNET believes in growing from within, and thus:
 Jordanian candidates shall be given preference to progress to the next step
throughout the different phases of the R&S process in case they possess
the same level of competence as others
 GHD|EMPHNET is committed to maintain confidentiality throughout the
recruitment process where all job applications, applicants’ documents and
information shall be treated in strict confidence, and access to such shall be
limited to concerned and authorized employees.
5. All recruitment requests shall be submitted at least 45 days prior to the anticipated/
required joining date.
6. The recruitment and selection process starts when the authorized concerned
Director/Team Leader reports the need to fill a vacancy to the Executive Director
through the identified means for the vacancies not listed in the Manpower plan,
while the HR Specialist will start the process for the vacancies that are listed in
the Manpower plan.
7. The possibility of promotion in vacancies within managerial levels should be
examined before starting the recruitment process. In case promotion is to be

considered, the adopted Human Resources Policies and Procedures in that
regard shall be followed.
8. The recruitment methods are categorized depending on the sources of candidates
into either internal or external recruitment. However, internal and external are
equally treated.
9. Internal and External Recruitment shall be pursued until at least 3 candidates are
provided.
10. Reference check shall be made for new employees if requested from the hiring
committee
11. Where screening relies on the compliance with the essential criteria of the
specifications profile, shortlisting depends on outcomes that differentiate between
candidates.
12. All candidates must fulfill the following before permanent appointment in
GHD|EMPHNET:
 To meet all essential job requirements as specified in the designated Job
Description Card
 To pass all oral and written tests specified for the designated job (if any), as well
as personal interviews
 For English Placement test, the candidate is considered successfully passed
the test if his/ her results met the reference level as detailed in Attachment 14.
 To obtain and submit all required documents and certificates requested by the
HR department
13. Communication with Candidates through the recruitment cycle:
 Once the applicant submit the job application, a thank you email shall be shared
with the candidate regarding his job application submission.
 Candidates who were not shortlisted to be interviewed shall receive an apology
email not more than 3 weeks after the closing of the announcement.
 Candidates who are going to be on-hold for a period of more than one month or
who are rejected after the interviews must be informed of such within two weeks
of last interaction.
More details regarding the Application cycle steps and timeline is illustrated in
Attachment 13.
14. The endorsement of appointing a candidate is the authority of the Executive
Director.
15. In Internal Recruitment, if a candidate is applying to a position that required to
perform any tests as part of the selection process in GHD|EMPHNET, he/she then
shall perform the required test(s).
16. GHD|EMPHNET shall bear all expenses related to the travel of candidates
residing outside Jordan or in a different location than that designated for the
interview, including accommodation expenses if an overnight stay was deemed
necessary.
17. The HR Department shall maintain accurate records of the conducted tests and
interviews for future reference.

18. Preferred external recruitment sources are specified for each Managerial Level as
follows:

middle or top management positions; first interview with the concerned Direct
Manager and the HR Manager, while the second interview will be with the
recruitment & selection committee. Whereas for entry level positions only 1

approved to recruit a new employee with the level of Manager/Specialist and

21. Where impartiality could be questioned, a member of the Recruitment & Selection
Committee shall withdraw in respect of a certain candidate in situations that the

or the member is or was a partner, employer, employee of the candidate in the
past five years.
22. Upon joining the organization, the employee passes through an orientation that is
conducted by the concerned parties. Where, new employee is provided with
GHD|EMPHNET essential documents, information and presentations to help new
employees feel welcomed, integrated into the organization, link them to helpful
knowledge and resources, as well as guiding them through their journey at
GHD|EMPHNET.
23. Before the end of the 3 months probationary period, The HR Officer sends the
employee evaluation form to the employee’s Direct Manager to evaluate
employee’s performance and examine how well he/she was able to conduct their
assigned duties and responsibilities.
24. The final decision could be successful completion of probationary period; if the
employee proves eligible and competent at his/her new position, or termination, if
the result of the evaluation was unsatisfactory or in case of misconduct.
25. Transfer and Assignments:
 Employee transfer might occur under the following cases:
 Employees are performing in a satisfactory manner in their current jobs,
hence the need arises to transfer those with special skills and experience to
a new position to utilize these special skills.
 Employees are not meeting performance expectations, if the transfer
provides them with a chance to better utilize their skills and abilities.
 An employee may have become dissatisfied with the job due to conflicts
with co-workers or his/her direct manager that appears to be irresolvable or
to be a dead-end job.
 Organizational needs, such as turnover, promotions and terminations may
result in job vacancies that may be filled most effectively through transfers
 Organizational or structural changes, such as downsizing the organization
which shall lead to a growing emphasis on lateral transfers for employee
development and broadening skills.
 The relocation and transfer of employees between various regions/locations
and across country (as applicable) to fill in employment gaps or to transfer
certain required expertise.
 The date of appointment of the transferred employee with the GHD|EMPHNET
remains unchanged.
 The final approval of the new direct manager for the transferred employee shall
be obtained after spending a period of three months in the new position.
 The transferred employee receives the salaries and benefits granted to him by
GHD|EMPHNET according to his new position.
 If the employee is transferred to a job of lower grade and/or salary, no changes
shall take place in the employee's current grade and salary.

 The employee shall not be transferred from his original workplace to another
place that entails a change in his place of residence if such transfer is likely to
cause serious harm to the employee and is not justified by the nature of work.
Business Assignment: The employee assigned to perform other duties besides
his original job is not entitled to any raises or bonuses for performing these
additional tasks; however, GHD|EMPHNET will provide flight tickets,
accommodation and transportation for assigned employees to outside Jordan
based on the shortest direct distance between workplace and assignment
place.
26. Any rehiring to the resigned employees should comply to the below rules &
regulations:
 The departure period should not be less than 12 – 18 months according to the
nature of the work.
 Any rehiring should be subjected to the availability and announcement of the
vacancy & work needs.
 The rehiring should be approved by a committee nominated by the HR
employee’s selection committee and endorsed by the ED.
 The performance of the rehired candidate through the past years should at
least reach the rank of 80% and above.
 The rehired candidate should not be terminated from his position because of
weak performance or Code of Conduct violation or any disciplinary action.
 The last salary entitled for the rehired candidate will not be considered but
based on the new open vacancy requirements & scale.
27. Work Permits:
 For full time employees whom nationality is other than Jordanian, then work
permit/ work residency shall be issued based on the working regulations in the
country.
 Work permits shall be followed closely and renewed on regular basis.
 Work permits shall be canceled upon employee contract end.
 All documents shall be kept at the employee’s file.
28. HR team shall notify GHD|EMPHNET employees upon new employee
recruitment, upon any change to the status of the employee such as title change,
promotion, new assignment.

nodes.heading: 2.1 purpose
nodes.own_text:
The purpose of the Performance Appraisal (PA) system is to offer a fair and balanced
review and appraisal of GHD|EMPHNET employee’s performance during their
contract period.

nodes.heading: 2.2 Scope
nodes.own_text:
The Performance Appraisal (PA) system is applied for all full-time employees at
GHD|EMPHNET.

nodes.heading: 2.3 Responsibilities
nodes.own_text:
The responsibility of implementing the PA falls upon the HR Department, as well as
the employee’s direct manager and Concerned Director/ Team Leader. The reason
behind this joint responsibility is to ensure that the process is being performed
according to the approved procedures via formal interaction with each appraiser.

nodes.heading: 2.4 Policies
nodes.own_text:
The employee performance appraisal seeks to achieve the following:
 Giving the employee and the direct manager the opportunity to set the
employee goals’ and expected accomplishments during the contract period.
 Reviewing employee performance effectively in an objective and fair
manner.
 Identifying employees' concealed potentials to ascertain the possibility of
adding more responsibilities or recommending transfer to a more
challenging position.
 Identifying weaknesses in performance and ensuring their treatment
through employee development forming a key input to training needs
assessment.
 Detecting mismatches between job-holders and their positions, hence
assisting in improving the recruitment and selection process.
 Increasing motivation and satisfaction levels among employees, thus
boosting morale which has positive impact on quality of work and
productivity.
2.
The employee performance appraisal should be carried out Annually; through
initiating the process on the Mena-Me HR system. While performance review will
be carried out semiannually.
Human Resources shall initiate the process of performance review in the middle
of contract, this evaluation is considered as a middle evaluation to make sure that
employee’s performance effectively archives the preset objectives. In addition, it
gives an opportunity for both the Direct Manager and employees to share any
comments, recommendations, requirements and challenges. Objectives could be
updated accordingly.

The employees are evaluated based on their performance related to their duties,
responsibilities, competencies, behavior, and relations with other employees.
The direct manager should be aware of the employee performance during the
performance appraisal period in terms of his/ her duties and responsibilities.
6.
In case the employee has more than one Direct Manager during the appraisal
period, then all concerned managers should participate in the employee
performance appraisal if the working period under each Direct manager is
reasonable (3 months and above).
The performance appraisal should take into consideration the whole performance
appraisal period not only part of it, and it should focus on the performance and
accomplishments.
The PA will be officially applied for all new employees who join GHD|EMPHNET
5 months prior to the launching to the Performance Appraisal.
When setting the performance goals, both the employee and his/her Direct
Manager should ensure that the goals are SMART:
 Specific: the goal should be clearly defined.
 Measurable: the goal is measurable so that direct manager has tangible
evidence that the employee met/ partially met/ not met the goal
 Achievable: humanly possible and has all the required resources.
 Realistic: within the availability of resources, knowledge and time. Also;
relevant to the employee's role, skills and qualifications
 Time bounded: set deadlines and enough time to achieve the desired goal.
10. The set goals of each employee will be evaluated based on three rating
descriptors:

Met the goal (100%)

Partially met the goal (1%-99%)

Not met the goal (0%)
11. Employee performance during the appraisal period will be evaluated based on 4
main criteria each is divided into sub criterion, the elements and their weights will
be based on the employee level/ position:

Soft Skills (6 elements)
Reliability/ Accountability
Civility and respect
Communication Skills
Relationship with co-workers
Taking Initiative
Teamwork


Commitment / Work Habits (3 elements)
Respect to work culture
Adherence to internal rules and regulations
Attendance/ Punctuality

Leadership & Management (7 elements)
Coaching & Mentoring
Decision Making
Relationship Building
Strategic Thinking
Problem Solving
Creativity & Innovation
Analytical Thinking

Work Performance (7 elements)
Timeliness of work delivered
Productivity
Quality of work delivered
Stakeholders’ satisfaction with work
Ability to plan and prioritize
Knowledge of work processes and procedures
Job Knowledge
12. Employee performance during the appraisal period will be evaluated based
on five rating descriptors:
 Outstanding (5): Performance far exceeded expectations due to
exceptionally high quality of work performed in all essential areas of
responsibility, resulting in an overall quality of work that was superior.
 Meets Expectations (4): Performance consistently meet expectations in
all essential areas of responsibility, and the quality of work overall was
excellent.
 Somehow below Expectations (3): Performance consistently do meet
minimum standards of acceptability in all essential areas of responsibility
 Improvement Needed (2): Performance did not consistently meet
expectations – performance failed to meet expectations in one or more
essential areas of responsibility. A professional development plan to
improve performance must be set
 Unsatisfactory (1): Performance was consistently below expectations in
most essential areas of responsibility. Significant improvement is needed
in one or more important areas. A plan to correct performance must be
set.
13. The Direct Manager should consider facts in the performance appraisal and
conduct it in a fair and objective manner.

14. The employee participates in his/her performance appraisal by setting annual
goals, in agreement with his/her direct manager, exchanging suggestions and
recommendations, as well as reviewing the evaluation results and appealing
on the performance appraisal (if needed).
15. If any direct manager gives the employee a rating of ‘Outstanding’ or
‘Unsatisfactory’ on any of the performance criteria elements, then a
commentary supporting such a rating must be provided. Although the direct
manager is still able to include comments on any evaluation criterion of the
PA form for the ratings (Exceeds Expectations, Meets Expectations,
Improvement Needed).
16. The results of the PA system are considered important inputs for the
employee training needs.

20. All employees eligible for promotions at GHD|EMPHNET shall be covered by

nodes.heading: 3.1 Purpose
nodes.own_text:
To provide instructions and steps needed to renew/end employment of a contracted
employee with GHD|EMPHNET according to the conditions of employment specified
in the contract. As well as to standardize the process of accepting/rejecting employees’
resignations while ensuring that all work requirements are met, all relevant documents
completed, and entitlements paid, in order to make sure that all employees are treated
in accordance with Jordanian Labor Law and the HR Policies and Procedure Manual.

nodes.heading: 3.2 Scope
nodes.own_text:
This section is applicable on all current employees who have an employment contract
with GHD|EMPHNET, whether their contracts will be renewed/ terminated, or they are
not welling to continue/ renew their employment with GHD|EMPHNET.

nodes.heading: 3.3 Responsibilities
nodes.own_text:
It is the primary responsibility of the Human Resource Department to coordinate and
implement the processes of employees’ contract renewal, ending, and resignation.
To coordinate between the dismissed employee and all other Departments to
ensure a smooth and professional exit process.
To ensure the overall completion of the resignation in coordination with the
concerned Teams/Departments as well as a smooth handover is taking place
during the notice period.
To coordinate between the employee, Direct Manager, and the Team
Leader/Director to ensure a smooth and professional contract renewal
process.

nodes.heading: 3.4 Policies
nodes.own_text:
-Upon contract end for any reason, the Direct Manager shall determine the faith of
the employee email, whether to be deactivated, sharing the emails back up with any
employee, keep the email active and to be assigned to the Direct Manager or to one
of the team.
- If the email is assigned to anyone, this should be clearly documented. And should
be re-evaluated after three months with the Direct Manager.
- Upon exit interview, the employee shall be informed politely to exit the WhatsApp
group after last day of employment. Otherwise, the employee shall be removed from
the group(s) after one week form last day of employment.
- HR team shall notify GHD|EMPHNET employees upon employees resignation one
week prior the end date, and to specify the new point of contact.
- Employees are requested to bring social security status upon contracts renewal.

GHD|EMPHNET has the right to terminate/not renew a contract with an
employee, provided that the employee gets all his entitlements, in the
occurrence of one of these cases:
1. If the employee does not perform his/her duties to an acceptable standard, then
he may be subject to termination because of not fulfilling essential job
conditions, and if GHD|EMPHNET is convinced that the employee made an
effort to perform the job, then the service of employee can be terminated while
still receiving his/her entitlements.
2. If the employee attains the age for retirement (60 years for males and 55 years
for females), and GHD|EMPHNET finds no need to renew the work contract
with the concerned employee.
3. Unfit medical status based on qualified medical reports.
4. Completing the period of employment contract.
GHD|EMPHNET has the right to terminate/not renew the contract with the
employee without advance notice, in the following cases:
1. If the employee fails to pass his probationary period.
2. If the employee shall assume the character or identity of the other or shall
submit forged certificates or documents aiming at bringing a benefit for himself
or a determent of others.
3. If the employee fails to satisfy his/her work duties and liabilities pursuant to the
employment contract.
4. If the employee commits a mistake that shall cause a gross material loss to the
employer provided that the employer shall report the accident to the competent
party or parties within five days of the date on which he shall know of the
incident.
5. If the employee violates the Internal Working Policy including the safety
conditions of the workplace and its employees.
6. If the employee uses his/her position and authority for personal benefits or gain.
7. If the employee is absent without having a valid excuse for more than twenty
discontinuous days through the one year or more than ten continuous days.
Provided that the dismissal shall be preceded by a written warning to be sent
by registered mail addressed to his address in addition to being published one
time in one of the daily local newspapers.
8. If the employee discloses any of GHD|EMPHNET’s documents and/or
Information
9. Accepting any type of gifts or bribes either tangible or intangible.
10. If the employee is convicted of a crime or an offense that encroaches the honor
and public morals of GHD|EMPHNET by virtue of a final court ruling.
11. If the employee is found in a drunken state or under the influence of a drug or
any mental capacity impediments or has committed an act that would be
against the public morals at the workplace while performing his/her duty.

12. If the employee physically, verbally or in writing assaults his/her employer,
direct manager, any of his/her department heads, any employee or any other
person while performing his/her duty or reason of his/her work.
13. If damning evidence was found that the employee is working with another
employer during his/her service with GHD|EMPHNET, even after the official
working hours.
14. Collecting donations without permission.
15. Seeking to establish direct relations with GHD|EMPHNET’s stockholders or
agencies outside the professional framework or seeking to compete against
GHD|EMPHNET while still on the job.
Employee has the right to terminate the contract with the GHD|EMPHNET,
according to the following guidelines:
1. The employee has the right to terminate the employment contract in
accordance with the Jordanian Labor Law, provided that the employee gives
a 30-day notice before the intended resignation date.
2. The GHD|EMPHNET employee who wishes to resign should submit a written
letter of resignation (Plain paper should be used) or send an official email
addressed to his/her Direct Manager keeping HR Manager in the loop.
3. A resignation letter is considered approved if it has the signature of the
Executive Director.
4. If the employee works during the notice period, then the effective day of the
termination would be the last day of the notice period.
5. If GHD|EMPHNET asks the employee to work during his notice period, and the
employee could not work the whole notice period, then the effective day of
termination would be the last day worked from the notice period.
6. If GHD|EMPHNET management asks the employee not to work during the
notice period, then the effective date of termination would be the date of
handing the termination notice (Resignation).
7. Exit Interview Questionnaire:
The resigned employee shall be shared with each employee to be filled and
shared back in his/ her last working week.
HRM shall be the only eligible employee to view and review the feedback
The responses shall remain confidential; however, the provided information
shall be used to improve and develop working environment and practice.
8. If the employee is subjected to probationary period, then both parties have the
right to terminate the work contract in consent.
9. If the employee and GHD|EMPHNET agree on such, the contract may be
terminated provided the employee’s consent is in writing.
The employee has the right to terminate the work contract without any previous
notice, in the following cases:
1. If GHD|EMPHNET fails to fulfill the contractual obligations and conditions
agreed upon and listed in the work contract.

2. If the employee is subjected to insult or assault from his/her managers or
superiors, then he/she has the right to terminate the contract.

nodes.heading: 4.1 Purpose
nodes.own_text:
The Training and Development system aims to develop and implement sufficient
GHD|EMPHNET goals and objectives through implementing several HR programs
and processes, ensure that all employees receive sufficient training that contributes to
developing their skills and enhancing their daily job performance, and assess and
identify the existing Competency gaps and the training needs on the individual,
functional and organizational levels.

nodes.heading: 4.2 Scope
nodes.own_text:
The Training and Development System outlines the process of identifying, estimating,
prioritizing training needs and developing training plans that are applicable to all the
employees at GHD|EMPHNET. It also defines the procedures and criteria of
suggesting, requesting, and evaluating training.

nodes.heading: 4.3 Responsibilities
nodes.own_text:
1. It is the responsibility of the HR Team in cooperation with Directors/Team
Leaders to develop and update a consistent Annual Training Plan.
2. It is the responsibility of the HR Team in cooperation with Directors/Team
Leaders to assess and prioritize training needs.
3. It is the responsibility of the HR Team in cooperation with all GHD|EMPHNET’s
concerned Directors, Direct Managers, and Employees to request a training
outside approved training plan.
4. It is the responsibility of the HR Team in cooperation with all GHD|EMPHNET’s
concerned Direct Managers/Team Leader and Employees to evaluate the
effectiveness and benefit of a specific training activity and its compliance to the
Organization’s objectives and policies.

nodes.heading: 4.4 Policies
nodes.own_text:
1. The training and development system should include a group of procedures for
implementing training in a manner that ensures meeting training needs and
adapting to technological and organizational changes.

2. The training and development system should ensure that all employees receive
sufficient training that contributes to developing their skills and enhancing their
daily job performance, thus, enabling them to carry out their duties safely and
without risk to themselves or others.
3. GHD|EMPHNET is committed to align training activities with its goals and
strategic plans and direct it towards supporting individual and organizational
performance and provide an effective liaison with local and international training
Vendor organizations.
4. GHD|EMPHNET is committed to distribute training resources equally among
employees to ensure progress and professional growth of all employees and
internal equity among employees in their training opportunities.
5. GHD|EMPHNET shall allocate an annual training budget as part of the
organization identified budget.
6. GHD|EMPHNET staff who is eligible for training and development must have
worked for GHD|EMPHNET for a minimum of nine months before they qualify
for any training, unless the training is dedicated to new employees or a
prerequisite for job performance, such as technical training. In this case, the
trainee shall be provided with a complete training course schedule.
7. A training report must be submitted within 2 weeks from the date the employee
completes a training course. Employees will not be recommended for another
training course unless their report for the previous course was submitted in a
timely manner and within acceptable standards.
8. Employees who completed a training course and in coordination with their
Direct Supervisors shall share the knowledge and skills acquired through
training, where applicable, by an elaborated presentation about the training
course or on-job Training (OJT).
9. On Quarterly basis, the HR Officer shall prepare a training report for the
implemented trainings that will address the following areas:
 Total cost per employee, Division, Department, Section or Unit.
 Performance of training institutions.
 Evaluation of the training process as per the defined criteria.
10. A record of all training courses provided for each employee will be held in the
employee's file at the Human Resources department. A record of courses

applied for and attended with a certificate of attendance or achievement of each
course, should be found in this file.
11. Training is performed according to the following stages:
 Development Stage: in this stage, training needs are assessed on the
organizational, occupational and individual levels. In addition, training
objectives are determined, vendors are selected, and training plans are
developed in this stage.
 Implementation Stage: this stage includes the selection of training
contents and the implementation of training courses that meet the
identified training needs.
 Evaluation Stage: in this stage, certain criteria are used to determine if
the training has achieved the desired objectives.
12. HR Manager, in coordination with Directors and Managers, shall conduct and
supervise TNA on the organizational level through carrying-out an
organizational analysis to analyze organization-wide performance.
13. The organizational training need analysis shall be conducted on yearly basis
(October), and the input shall be from the individualized basis based on the
Performance Appraisal and from on division/ departmental basis based on the
feedback from the Team Leaders and Directors . However, the analysis of
major problems on the organizational level shall be conducted when they occur
in order to determine whether these problems can be partially or completely
resolved by training.
14. Direct managers shall recommend on-job training (OJT) that focuses on
methods to perform the task efficiently, safely and economically.
15. The Human Resources department shall prioritize the training needs in
coordination with Division Directors and Team Leaders and accordingly decide
on the priorities of the Division or Department budget allocation based on the
following factors respectively:
 Training needs on the organizational level.
 Training courses needed to perform the job as per the job description.
 Training needs on the individual level.
16. The HR Manager in coordination with employee Direct Manager will determine
the needed training workshops and whether they should be in-house training or
public training.

17. Each Direct Manager shall ensure that the training courses' contents and
objectives proposed by training vendors meet the Division/Department needs
and address the gap between actual and desired performance. This is achieved
by evaluating the extent to which the training course covers training needs.
18. The trainee shall send copies of the training report to his/ her Direct Manager
and to the HR Officer. A copy of the training material will be submitted within
two weeks of the date of course end to enable others to share the knowledge,
or for the purpose of research and development.
19. Based on the training nature, trainings could be conducted by external vendor
or internal employee/ team.
20. No reimbursement is acceptable for trainings unless prior approval was given
by GHD|EMPHNET.

nodes.heading: 5.1 Purpose
nodes.own_text:
To provide a system within GHD|EMPHNET for monitoring and controlling employee
vacations, leaves, regular attendance, and punctuality in a manner which ensures
the sustainability of work activities and accomplishments.

nodes.heading: 5.2 Scope
nodes.own_text: This procedure applies to all full-time employees at GHD|EMPHNET.

nodes.heading: 5.3 Responsibilities
nodes.own_text:
1. It is the responsibility of Human Resources team to monitor employees’ working
hours, analyze and manage employees’ monthly attendance sheet and to
propose solutions to any attendance issues.
2. The HR Manager is responsible for sending a monthly Employee Attendance
Logs to the Financial & Admin Affairs Director at GHD|EMPHNET, as per the
current HR-adopted system.
3. Managers are responsible for monitoring the daily attendance of their team
members.
4. Managers are responsible for informing the HR team by email of employee
absences.
5. GHD|EMPHNET employees are responsible for recording their actual times of
departure and return of business and personal leaves using the Mena HR
system and the attendees scanner.
6. The HR team is responsible for the implementation of all relevant policies and
procedure.
7. Direct managers are responsible for the preparation and planning of their team
members’ annual vacations in a manner which sustains the levels of
productivity and tasks achievement. This includes the decision to obtain and
assign a substitute for the vacationing employee if necessary.
8. The HR Department is responsible for studying annual vacation plans and
ensuring their consistency with due dates and vacation balances.
9. The human resources team in consultation and coordination with the respective
team leader, should be responsible for implementing working from anywhere
policy and for ensuring commitment and adherence.
10. It is the direct manager’s responsibility to ensure that work commitments are
provided for when considering the personal needs of each employee's leave
request. Managers must consider providing a substitute employee to handle
the duties and responsibilities of the vacationing employee to ensure that
his/her absence does not cause work dissatisfaction whilst also avoiding the
accumulation of outstanding leave.

11. It is the responsibility of the Human Resources Manager to monitor annual
leave entitlements and ensure they are taken within contract period.

nodes.heading: Employee Attendance
nodes.own_text:
1. Working hours for GHD|EMPHNET employees must not exceed 48 hours per
week with a maximum of 10 hours per day. During the month of Ramadan, the
actual working hours shall be reduced to a maximum of six hours a day or thirty-
six hours per week.
2. Each employee of GHD|EMPHNET must have at least one day of rest per
week. For GHD|EMPHNET, this day is Friday. Though Saturdays are usually
non-working days, occasionally employees may be requested to work on
Saturday as deemed necessary according to the load of work. Should this be
the case, management will notify the employee(s) who are requested to work
on a specific Saturday and the employee(s) must comply accordingly without
requesting any compensation.
3. GHD|EMPHNET follows the official holidays announced by the Jordanian
Government.
4. GHD|EMPHNET employees shall use the specified entrances and exits and
shall arrive and leave work at the defined times that are communicated to them
including daily arrival and departure times and scheduled shift times (if
applicable).
5. All GHD|EMPHNET employees shall use the attendance scanner located at
GHD|EMPHNET’s entrances to record the times of their arriving and departing
the work premises.
6. The daily working hours of GHD|EMPHNET employees shall not be less than
8 hours a day, including the lunch break.
a. Flexible working hours are from 8:30 a.m. – 5:30 p.m. each employee
has to attend at least 8 hours daily between these hours to accumulate
8 hours of attendance on every working day. However, the working hours
for Financial & Administrative Affairs is for 08:30 a.m. – 05:00 p.m.
7. GHD|EMPHNET employees should arrive to work before 9:30 a.m. and shall
not leave work before 4:30 p.m.
8. Regular late check-ins after 9:30 a.m. and/or early check-outs before 4:30 p.m.
are considered a violation of the attendance policy and will be handled in
accordance with the type of violation identified in the Internal bylaw.
9. The total time of Late Attendance after 9:30 a.m. and/or Early Departure and/or
not meeting the required 8 working hours per day will be automatically deducted
from the employee’s annual vacation balance. In cases when the employee
does not have enough vacation balance, deduction will be made from the
employee’s monthly salary equaling to the delay time for that month.

10. GHD|EMPHNET employees with special personal conditions/circumstances
needing to obtain an exception regarding the official work times shall
communicate the need to the HR Manager.
11. Final approval regarding exceptions to the official working hours is subject to
the approval of the Executive Director and is based upon the recommendations
of the employee's direct manager and next level manager (Team
Leader/Director).
12. Late attendance, early departure, and not using the attendance scanner in
checking in/ out, personal leave and business leave from work will be handled
in accordance with the internal bylaw.
13. Working hours and rest periods during the day are scheduled so that no
employee works for more than five consecutive hours without an entitled half-
hour break for rest and meals during the total working hours.
14. Lunch/Meal breaks are essential to good health and performance and should
generally be no more than 30 minutes long. Accordingly lunch must be taken
between 12:30pm to 01:30pm.
15. Break times shall not be used to compensate attendance hours for late arrival
or early check-out.
16. Any employee who leaves GHD|EMPHNET offices during the break time shall
check out and in to record the time of departure and arrival back to the office.
17. GHD|EMPHNET employees shall take their lunches in the cafeteria at the 4th
floor provided that their lunches do not leave any residue or offensive odor that
will negatively impact other employees.
18. GHD|EMPHNET employees leaving the office during the daily break times shall
check out and in to record the times of departure and arrival back to the office.
19. Occasionally lunch/mealtimes may be rotated to ensure that employees’
lunchtimes vary. Regularly taking long and/or late lunches will not be tolerated
and will result in having the time not worked deducted from the employees’
annual vacation balance and further handled in accordance with the internal
bylaw.
20. When employees are late, they are required to contact their managers
personally and advise them of their lateness and their estimated time of arrival.
It is not acceptable to call a fellow worker, email the office. Constant and
continual lateness will not be tolerated and will be considered an action of
violation.
21. Absence from work without reason or official permission is a violation of the
rules set forth in this section and will be considered absent without excuse and
the time will be deducted from the employee’s annual vacation balance.
22. Policies (1- 21) do not apply to the following cases, subject to the approval of
the Executive Director:
a. Work that is intermittent by necessity.
b. Employees who, through the nature of their work, are required to be out
of GHD|EMPHNET offices before or after the time of signing in or out.

nodes.path: Section 05 > 5.4 Policies > Personal Leave and Annual Vacations
nodes.heading: Personal Leave and Annual Vacations
nodes.own_text:
s
1. All GHD|EMPHNET permanent employees, after probation period, are entitled
a total of 10 hours of personal leave per month or three weeks (15 working
days) paid annual leave accrued on a pro-rata basis, and employees much take
their annual leave “vacation” during the contract period.
2. Personal leave should be limited to the minimum time required to complete the
personal job. Personal leave should not exceed 3 hours each time and should
not be less than 30 minutes each time.
3. If any of the personal leaves exceeds 3 hours, then a one-day vacation (8
hours) shall be deducted from the concerned employee annual vacation
4. Accumulating eight hours of personal leave time will be considered the same
as a one-day vacation (8 hours) and will be deducted from the concerned
employee’s annual vacation balance.
5. If an employee exceeded amount of time of late check-ins and/or personal
leaves has also depleted the employee’s annual vacation balance, the
exceeded time shall then be deducted from the employee’s salary.
6. Prior to the actual time of taking a personal leave, an employee must first take
permission from his/her direct manager and must apply and request the leave
on the Mena-Me HR System.
7. If a direct manager denies approval of personal leave requests, they shall
communicate a reasonable cause for denying the request to the concerned
employee.
8. A GHD|EMPHNET employee shall not leave the office before obtaining the
approval of his/her direct manager except in cases of emergency.
9. The direct manager must ensure that employees are not abusing their right to
a personal leave.
10. GHD|EMPHNET employees are eligible for an annual vacation only after
completion of the probation period at GHD|EMPHNET; the employee shall refer
to his next level manager if he/she needs to take an annual vacation before the
end of the probation period.
11. Employees under probation are not entitled for any kind of leave during their
probationary period, but once the probation ends, the vacation days
accumulated during that period will be added to employee balance of vacation.
12. All annual vacation requests with duration exceeding two days shall be
submitted at least one week ahead of the vacation’s starting date. However, if
the request was submitted in less than one week from the requested vacation’s
starting date, the Executive Director may approve vacation requests with
durations exceeding two days on a case-by-case basis.
13. GHD|EMPHNET has the right to plan vacations according to its work
requirements; however, it shall respect the right of its employees to set the date
of their annual vacations.

14. Employees’ annual vacation days shall be specified according to the signed
contract between EMPHNET and the employee where each employee will be
entitled to a minimum 1.25 days of paid vacation for each month of service.
15. Every employee with three years of service or more at GHD|EMPHNET is given
a total of 21 working days of annual vacation according what is mentioned in
the contract upon renewal.
16. If an official holiday falls during a period when an employee is absent from work
or the employee is sick and takes paid sick leave for the period of their illness,
the employee’s annual leave accrual will not be reduced by that day or period.
17. GHD|EMPHNET employees are not allowed to request an annual vacation that
exceeds the accrued annual vacation balance until the end of the vacation
period.
18. An GHD|EMPHNET employee shall not start the requested vacation before
obtaining the approval of his/her direct manager except in cases of emergency.
19. In special circumstances, and according to work conditions, GHD|EMPHNET
may contact an employee on vacation to discuss the possibility of shortening or
cancelling the vacation altogether to overcome these circumstances.
GHD|EMPHNET will compensate the employee by adding the remaining days
from his/her annual vacation to his/her vacation balance.
20. An employee cannot accumulate any annual vacation balance and must use all
of his/her vacation days during the contract period.
21. Any accumulated vacation balance that is not used before the end of the
contract will be discarded.
22. In deciding whether to authorize annual leave, GHD|EMPHNET is entitled to
take into account the operational requirements of the workplace. An employer
must not unreasonably:
 Refuse to authorize annual leave being taken; or
 Take back an authorization.

nodes.heading: Business Leave
nodes.own_text:
1. Sometimes an employee may be required to attend a meeting or a field activity.
Should this deem necessary, the employee should have prior approval from
his/her direct manager on the Mena-Me HR System.
2. Business leave without the approval of the direct manager will be considered
personal leave and will be deducted from the employee’s annual vacation
3. GHD|EMPHNET employees required to leave GHD|EMPHNET office on
business leave shall check out and in to record the times of departure and
arrival back to the office.
4. Non-compliance to the business leaves policies will not be tolerated and may
result in having the hours of the business leave deducted from an employees’
annual vacation balance and handled in accordance with the Discipline Manual.

5. If the employee was on travel assignments, then travel dates shall be added to
the Mena as Business leaves

nodes.heading: Working from Anywhere (WfA)
nodes.own_text:
1. WfA can be initiated by management or requested by employee for specific
reasons.
2. Management may apply WfA, hybrid module, Working from Office to
employees/ teams based on health status and/ or work requirements. Clear
instructions will be shared with employees regarding their working modules
3. Employees working from offices whose nature of their work does not require
them to be at the office is eligible for 6 days per month to work from anywhere.
4. Employee whose nature of work requires them to be located in a country, other
than those assigned to work directly with ministries/stakeholders is eligible for
6 days per month.
5. The following positions are not eligible for WfA requests: Accounting Manager,
Senior Accountant, Accountant, Junior Accountant, Treasury Accountant,
Logistics Supervisor, Logistics Officer, Maintenance Officer, Driver, Office
Assistant and Receptionist.
6. The Executive Director, based on the recommendation of the HR Manager,
teams leaders and Directors, will approve any future amendments needed,
including the list of all positions who are eligible for working from anywhere.
7. The Human Resources should be informed of all employees who will be
working from anywhere.
8. When working from anywhere, both employee and his/her direct manager
should set boundaries on work schedule and adhere to the official working
hours. The official working hours should not be less than 8 hours a day.
9. Working period is from 8:30 a.m. – 5:30 p.m. Eligible employees are expected
to be working 8 hours during this time and in agreement with their direct
manager.
10. All internal/Bi-weekly/one-on-one meetings should be scheduled to take place
during the organization’s core working hours (8:30 a.m. – 5:30 p.m.).
11. WfA employees should be accessible for using video conferencing with
Microsoft Teams or Zoom.
12. WfA employees are expected to be online and accessible for 8 hours, at least,
Sunday to Thursday. They are expected to check-in/ check-out three times a
day through the WFA system in the following durations:
 The first punch, check-in: from 08:30 till 09:30 hours.
 The second punch, recheck-in: from 12:30 till 13:30 hours.
 The third punch, check-out: from 16:30 till 17:30 hours.
13. WfA should not affect the mentoring and coaching responsibility of Managers,
Team Leaders, or Directors. Mangers, Team leaders and Directors need to do
one-on-one sessions with their respective teams to discuss strengths and
challenges in executing their role and related tasks.

14. While working from anywhere, employees must adhere to all HR policies. All
policies around conduct, confidentiality, sick leave, etc., continue to apply,
regardless of location.
15. While working from anywhere, employees must adhere to all IT policies. All
policies around data backup and confidentiality, security, and internet browsing,
phishing emails, installing software, maintaining hardware, continue to apply,
regardless of location.
16. Manager may ask to pull a poorly performing employee, working from
anywhere, back to the office or suspend his/her eligibility, when the Manager
sees that the employee needs more onsite/face-to-face coaching and
mentoring or when performance does not meet the expectations. All eligible
employees may work from anywhere for a maximum two consecutive days.
Employees are required to report and present themselves at the office on
weekly basis.
17. Country based employees utilizing this policy should communicate and agree
with their GHD|EMPHNET point of contact. Those who have the role of working
directly with the ministry/stakeholder are not eligible to WfA policy requests.
18. GHD|EMPHNET has the right to cease the WfA arrangement of any employee
if it adversely affects any aspect of its business operation.
19. The approved WfA request shall waive all rights to the legal obligations of
GHD|EMPHNET (in regard to occupational health and safety, workers
compensation, rehabilitation, public liability insurance to cover the possibility of
injury to third parties, etc.) for the employee while working from anywhere.
20. Once a WfA request has been signed and approved it must be adhered to.
Employee will be unable to amend the agreed working from anywhere
arrangement to holiday.
21. Employees shall submit their WfA request on the Mena system Approval of WfA
requests is the responsibility of the Direct Manager and then the Director. .

nodes.heading: Unpaid Vacation
nodes.own_text:
1. All Un-paid vacations are subject to the approval of the Executive Director.
2. GHD|EMPHNET could grant unpaid vacations for employees up to a maximum
of 20 days per year, under the following circumstances:
 If the employee exhausted all his/her annual vacation days.
 If the type of the leave needed does not match any of the leave types
available at GHDEMPHNET.
 The reason of the leave should be acceptable to GHD|EMPHNET, all
concerned management and HR.
 The vacation leave does not conflict with job requirements and the normal
operations of GHD|EMPHNET.
3. In times of emergency when the vacation balance of the employee in need of
vacation is insufficient, the Executive Director is entitled, upon the
recommendation of the concerned manager, to grant the employee an

emergency unpaid vacation, provided that the total vacation days taken do not
exceed 20 continuous or intermittent days. If an unpaid vacation exceeds the
permitted consecutive 20 days, the employment contract shall be deemed
suspended unless contractually agreed to otherwise.
4. Extending unpaid vacation (more than 20 days) is subject to the direct
manager recommendation and the Executive Director’s approval and based
on the job availability upon return or continuity of service.
5. In case of an emergency, the employee requesting a vacation shall be
provided with top priority to facilitate and complete all steps entailed in the
procedure in a timely and convenient manner.
6. In extraordinary and justifiable circumstances, leave without pay shall not be
granted:

When an employee has an entitlement to accrued or pro rata annual
leave

When work commitments cannot be met during the proposed leave.
7. When leave without pay is granted, in most cases continuity of service will be
retained; however, the period of leave without pay will not count towards
service. No guarantees can be made as to the availability of the employee's
existing position upon return from extended leave without pay. Long service,
annual leave and other service-related benefits shall all be suspended during
periods of leave without pay.
8. Payroll and Treasury team shall be notified upon unpaid vacation approval.

nodes.heading: Sick Leave
nodes.own_text:
1. The employee or his family shall promptly inform his/her direct manager by
phone if sick leave is due to an emergency/severe sickness.
2. GHD|EMPHNET employees are eligible for 14 days of sick leave a year with
full pay either continuous or intermittent.
3. If the employee need to take a day(s) sick leave, he/she should submit a
medical report from an accredited medical entity along with the Leave
Request, if not applicable at the same day, then the employee has the right to
submit the request within 48 hours from the leave.
4. When sick leave is not reported in advance, sick leave shall not exceed two
working days except in cases of emergency/ severe sickness, and approval
shall be decided by the concerned Manager upon a letter from the accredited
medical entity.
5. The first day in which the employee is turned over to the medical care as well
as the medical examination period shall be treated as sick leave days and
accordingly deducted from the sick leave balance.
6. Sick leave can be renewed for another fourteen days according to Jordanian
Labor Law and relevant acting Jordanian legislations.
7. If an employee becomes ill during vacation, the sick days will not be considered
a sick leave but will be deemed part of the employee’s annual vacation.

8. If the employee requests a sick leave to undergo treatment for a non-
emergency medical condition as certified by the accredited medical entity that
could be postponed until the employee takes his/her vacation, then the
employee would not be granted a paid sick leave.
9. For employees with extended sick leave, their case shall be handled according
to the active relevant legislations and according to labor law and social security
law.
10. For employees with extended sick leaves, and with accordance to the
Jordanian Labor Law, the employee compensation during his/her sickness
shall be as follows:

Full compensation during the first four weeks (28 days) of sick leave.

50% of compensation for the following four weeks (28 days) of sick leave.

No compensation for the following months.
11. As per the Jordanian Labor Law, should the sick leave extend to period totaling
13 weeks or above, and medical reports show that the employee suffers a
chronic illness with recovery taking much longer than 13 weeks,
GHD|EMPHNET has the right to terminate the employee under the terms of
disability related to the sickness.

nodes.heading: Official Holidays
nodes.own_text:
1. All employees are entitled to full holiday pay on religious and official holidays
and occasions announced by of the Jordanian Government.
2. Sometimes GHD|EMPHNET may request that employees work during official
holidays. For each holiday an employee works, 1.5 days will be added to the
employee’s vacation balance.

nodes.heading: Hajj Vacation
nodes.own_text:
1. Employees shall be entitled to a paid leave of 14 days to perform Hajj, granted
only once during an employee’s service.
2. To be eligible for this holiday, the employee must have spent at least 3
consecutive years with GHD|EMPHNET from their first contract date.
3. GHD|EMPHNET has the right to determine the number of workers who shall be
given this vacation annually in accordance with work requirements and taking
into consideration the number of years of the employee’s service at
GHD|EMPHNET.

nodes.heading: Emergency Vacation
nodes.own_text:
GHD|EMPHNET employees are entitled to the following emergency vacations that are
granted occasionally given that these do not exceed a total of six days spread over
one year for any of the following reasons and based on conditions imposed by
management. No two of the following case scenarios can be combine in the same
month, unless deemed appropriate by management:
1. Three days paid vacation because of marriage of employee.

2. Three days paid vacation given to the employee in the case of the death of one
of the first or second relatives (husband or wife, a parent, a son or daughter, a
brother or sister, a grandfather or grandmother, father- or mother-in-law). One
day vacation for the death of employee’s direct aunt or uncle.
3. Three days paid vacation is given to female employees if she must accompany
her child to the hospital upon providing proof via a medical report.
4. In any one of the following cases, a one day paid vacation is given to an
employee:
a.
Attendance of surgery for a blood-relative or next-of-kin family member
b.
Admission of a parent, child, or spouse to the hospital as their caretaker
c.
Death of an uncle, aunt, nephew, or niece
d.
A serious traffic accident involving a parent, husband, wife, child, or
sibling.
5. Any emergency leave requests for a reason not mentioned herewith shall
depend on the Executive Director’s directive. Otherwise, and if not reported
over the telephone or the Mena-Me HR system, absence with no reason will
be considered as absence without excuse. The penalty imposed will be taken
according to the sequence of penalties that will follow later, and the day will be
deducted from the employee annual vacation balance or salary of the employee
or will otherwise be kept at the discretion of management.

nodes.heading: Paternity Leave
nodes.own_text:
Three days paid vacation is given to GHD|EMPHNET male employees in case of Birth
of a child.

nodes.heading: Maternity Leave
nodes.own_text:
Female employees are entitled to the following:
1. Ten weeks (70 days) of maternity leave with full pay before and after childbirth
provided that the period after the childbirth shall not be less than six weeks.
2. One-year full-time vacation without pay to raise her children. However, if she works
elsewhere during this period, she might lose her right to return to work.
3. A breastfeeding period to breastfeed her newborn during working hours at full
payment for one year from the date of birth provided that this does not exceed one
hour per day.

nodes.heading: General
nodes.own_text:
1. Employees are not allowed to leave the office without having prior approval of
annual leave, personal leave, or business leave, and should submit the leave
request on the Mena-Me HR System.
2. Any vacation obtained without following the required procedure is deemed absence
without official reason and disciplinary action will be taken as appropriate.
3. An employee shall not work for another employer during at any point during his/her
leave/vacations.

4. If an employee is found working for another employer, GHD|EMPHNET may
consider it a cause for termination without any legal liability or take necessary
disciplinary action as it sees fit in direct coordination with the HR Manager and as
per the Jordanian labor law requirements.
5. Any other matters not mentioned are to be discussed and determined by the
management in accordance with the Jordanian Labor Law.

nodes.heading: Overtime
nodes.own_text:
1. Overtime approval is subject to Executive Director approval based on Employees
Direct Manager recommendations showing the work required to be
2. The maximum number of hours allowed for overtime work is two hours per day.
3. In case of emergency situations where taking prior approval is not possible due to
work requirements, then taking post approval is possible based on Employees’
Direct Manager recommendations detailing the required work and the emergency
case.
4. GHD|EMPHNET shall compensate overtime by adding 1.25 hours to the
employee’s annual vacation balance for each extra hour during regular working
days
5. GHD|EMPHNET shall compensate overtime by adding 1.5 hours to the employee’s
annual vacation balance for each extra hour during weekends and official holidays.
6. If the employee was on business travel outside his/ her base (residency), and an
official holiday (other than Friday and Saturday), then he/ she will be compensated
this day with a day off within one month from that day.
7. Overtime must be authorized in advance to the actual time it is needed to be
performed, excluding emergencies and urgent operational needs.
Employees should report actual extra hours using the adopted attendance recording
system as much as possible.

nodes.heading: 6.1 Purpose
nodes.own_text:
The purpose of Discipline procedures is to ensure the commitment and adherence
of all GHD|EMPHNET employees to the internal regulations and policies of
GHD|EMPHNET. While the Grievance procedure provide a system for grievance
process that ensures employee equity and fairness because of an internal act that
is perceived as causing injustice, personal work obstruction or violating work
policies and procedures affecting the employee. The complaint procedure aims to
provide fair, open and clear process for complaints and ensure a satisfactory
outcome for all GHD|EMPHNET employees.

nodes.heading: 6.2 Scope
nodes.own_text:
Discipline and Grievance are applicable to all prospective or current employees of
the GHD|EMPHNET. For the Discipline, the process starts when the Direct Manager
notices or is informed of a violation made by the employee till The HR Manager
formally notifies the employee of the violation that the employee committed in detail
and the disciplinary action taken against him/her. For the Grievance, the process
starts from submitting the grievance request until informing the employee of the
formal verdict of the grievance. The complaint policy starts when the employee
submit a complaint request until informing the employee of the formal verdict of the
complaint.

nodes.heading: 6.3 Responsibilities
nodes.own_text:
1. It is the responsibility of the Human Resources team to periodically updating
employees with internal bylaw, policies and regulations in addition to any
disciplinary actions related to their violation
2. The Human Resources Manager is responsible for the supervision of the
implementation of the Discipline, Grievance & Complaint policies.
3. It is the responsibility of the HR Department in cooperation with all
GHD|EMPHNET’s concerned Manager/ Team Leader & Director and the
Grievance Committee to conduct the grievance process.
4. It is the responsibility of the Human Resources to handle the employees’
complaints and to determine the disciplinary action after a deep investigation in
all the aspect of complaints received from the employees.

nodes.heading: 6.4 Policies
nodes.own_text:
Discipline:
1. GHD|EMPHNET acts against employees who are proven to be responsible for
committing violations such as those mentioned in internal bylaw, violating any

of the laws, regulations, policies or procedures applied at GHD|EMPHNET in
any form of disciplinary penalties, where a verbal or written notice or a first or
second written warning is issued, or a percentage is deducted of the daily wage
in addition to deducting late or absence penalties when they occur.
2. Employees shall be informed and continually updated with any new or updated
internal regulations and policies and the disciplinary actions related to their
violation.
3. The disciplinary actions applied at GHD|EMPHNET shall be in line with the ones
detailed in GHD|EMPHNET internal bylaw and in compliance with the
Jordanian Labor Law.
4. All disciplinary actions are not valid after 15 days after revealing the violation
and taking no action to investigate it.
5. An employee committing more than one violation at the same time shall be
disciplined with the highest disciplinary action of the consecutive committed
violations.
6. No more than one penalty is stated for each violation and no penalties are
added up.
7. Penalties are implemented only after informing the concerned employee about
the violation he/she committed and ensuring that he/she receives Violation
Notification of the related penalty he/ she is subject to. If he/ she refuses to
receive the document or sign it, two witnesses shall sign that the employee was
informed but refused to sign about the penalties.
8. GHD|EMPHNET employees shall be granted the chance to defend their cases
prior to imposing the penalties and such defenses shall be documented in
writing.
9. GHD|EMPHNET may not conduct any penalties for violations committed
outside the workplace unless it is directly related to the nature of work or
GHD|EMPHNET or its staff.
10. A warning shall cease to have effect on an employee upon the lapse of more
than 12 months after the date of such warning.
11. An employee who has been served two warnings shall be terminated if such an
employee commits any of the violations listed in the internal bylaw within the
effective period of the two warnings.
12. In addition to the penalties imposed by virtue of the internal bylaw; the employee
shall not be entitled to wages for the periods of delay or absence without leave.
13. A record for all employees’ violations are maintained at the HR Department,
including type of violations, date of committing violations, and related penalties.
14. Should the employee commit more than four violations of the same article, the
penalty of the fourth violation continues to apply. If the violation becomes a
serious trend, a committee of his direct manager, concerned Director, and the
HR Manager will be formed to decide on the proper disciplinary action in-line
with GHD|EMPHNET policies and procedures, keeping in mind that
GHD|EMPHNET has the right to discharge the employee after the second
warning.

15. In addition to the penalties stipulated in the internal bylaw, the administration
may:
a. Provided that the same is proven to be attributed to the employee’s
mistake or violation of the Administration’s instructions, deduct the value
of lost, damaged items or the value of their repair. The value of the
deduction shall not exceed three days’ wages per month.
b. Reserve its right of judicial recourse to claim for damages caused by the
employee.
16. Employment shall be terminated without notice in the following cases:
a. If the employee shall assume the character or identity of another or shall
submit forged certificates or documents aiming at bringing benefit for
himself or detriment of others.
b. If the employee fails to satisfy his work duties and liabilities pursuant to
the employment contract.
c. If the employee commits a mistake that shall cause a gross material loss
to the employer provided that the employer shall report the accident to
the competent party or parties within five days of the date on which he
knows of the incident.
d. If the Employee violates the internal working policy including the safety
conditions of the workplace and other employees.
e. If the employee uses his position and authority for personal benefits or
gain.
f. If the employee is absent without having a valid excuse for more than
twenty discontinuous days through the one year or more than ten
continuous days. Provided that the dismissal shall be preceded by a
written warning to be sent by registered mail addressed to his address
in addition to being published one time in one of the daily local
newspapers.
g. If the employee discloses any information about GHD|EMPHNET or its
documents.
h. Accepting any type of gifts or bribes, either tangible or intangible.
i. If the employee is convicted of a crime or an offense that encroaches
GHD|EMPHNET’s honor and public morals by virtue of a final court
ruling.
j. If the employee is found in a drunken state or under the influence of a
drug or any mental capacity impediments or has committed an act that
would be against the public morals at the work place while performing
his duty.
k. If the employee assaults, whether physically verbally or written, his/her
employer, direct manager, any of his/her department heads, any
employee or any other person while performing his duty or reason of
his/her work.

l. If damning evidence was found that the employee is working with
another employer during his service with GHD|EMPHNET, even after the
official working hours.
m. Collecting donations without permission.
n. Seeking to establish direct relations with GHD|EMPHNET’s partners or
agencies outside the professional framework or seeking to compete
against GHD|EMPHNET while still on the job.
17. If the employee wishes to grieve against the penalty, he/ she shall raise a
grievance request.
Grievance:
18. Due to the importance Grievance procedure as a means of sustaining
employee satisfaction and raising moral, all timeframes described within this
document shall be strictly enforced.
19. Employee shall be raised within a period of 15 days from the date of occurrence
of the cause of grievance.
20. Any employee with a grievance who requests any document shall not be denied
access, provided that the document directly relates to the subject of the
grievance and the employee has the authority to review these documents.
21. The period extending from the date the employee submitted his grievance until
the date of informing him of the formal verdict shall not exceed 15 working days.
22. If an employee needs to file a grievance against his direct manager, then the
grievance is to be filed with the next level manager.
23. If the grievance is against the HR team member, the Human Resources
Manager is responsible for carrying out the requirements of this procedure.
Complaints
24. The formal complaints policy is intended to ensure that all complaints are
handled fairly, consistently, and wherever possible resolved to the
complainant's satisfaction.
25. Official complaints is open to all GHD|EMPHNET employees.
26. Once receiving a formal complaint, the HR Manager should ensure the
following:
 Acknowledge the formal complaint in writing
 Respond within a stated period of time.
 Deal reasonably and sensitively with the complaint
 Take action where appropriate.
27. The complainant should ensure the following once decided to file a complaint:
 Send the complaint in writing to the identified email for
(complaint@emphnet.net) within 2 weeks of the issue arising
 Raise complaints promptly and directly
 Explain the problem as clearly and as fully as possible, including any
action taken to date

 Allow the HR Department and Management a reasonable time to deal
with the matter
 Recognize that some circumstances may be beyond GHD|EMPHNET
control.
28. The HR Manger in coordination with the ED shall formulate the Complaints
Committee based on the case and the situation.
29. Confidentiality shall be maintained throughout the processes, and information are
shared only with the involved people and according to their level of involvement.

nodes.heading: 7.1 Purpose
nodes.own_text:
To provide GHD|EMPHNET employees with important information covering policies,
procedures, definitions, acronyms for health insurance, experience/employment/ to
whom it may concern/ salary letter and recommendation letter issuance.

nodes.heading: 7.2 Scope
nodes.own_text: Applies to all prospective or current employees of the GHD|EMPHNET.

nodes.heading: 7.3 Responsibilities
nodes.own_text:
1. It is the responsibility of the Human Resource team to enroll the
GHD|EMPHNET’s employees with the health insurance plan, and to coordinate
the overall process between the GHD|EMPHNET’s employees and the health
insurance company.
2. It is the responsibility of the Human Resources Department to issue
Experience/Employment/To whom it may Concern and Salary Letters upon an
employee’s request.
3. It is the responsibility of the Human Resources Department in cooperation with
the concerned Direct Manager, and Director to issue recommendation letter
upon an employee’s request.

nodes.heading: 7.4 Policies
nodes.own_text:
Health Insurance
1. GHD|EMPHNET covers its employees who want to join the health insurance and
their family (Wife/ husband and children) through including them in one of the
insurance companies working in Jordan according to the approved insurance
policy, after successfully completing the probation period.
2. GHD|EMPHNET pays full membership for health insurance of its employees their
families (Wife/ husband and children) and shall not bear the cost of any medical,
surgical, or other services that are not included in the medical insurance plan.
3. All employees shall abide by all rules, conditions, terms, and restrictions mentioned
in the medical insurance policy available at GHD|EMPHNET.
4. Once a GHD|EMPHNET employee contract is ended, then the employee shall
return all the insurance related items to the human resources.
5. GHD|EMPHNET employees traveling on business assignments shall be issued
travel medical insurance prior to the travel date unless it is required earlier for visa
issuance.
6. GHD|EMPHNET employees traveling on monthly basis and/or for long business
trips (more than five times a year) especially to certain countries shall have annual
travel medical insurance or as decided by GHD|EMPHNET.

7. The duration of travel medical insurance shall cover the expected duration of the
business trip.
Care Program:
1. To support the community and (Cancer Care Program) and to encourage its
employees, GHD|EMPHNET covers part of membership fees for (Cancer Care
Program) for the employees and their families (Wife/ husband and children).
2. through an ongoing agreement with King Hussain Cancer Center (KHCC). in
(to include all its employees and their families in the Cancer Care Program
(CCP)).
3. All GHD|EMPHNET employees and their families are eligible to be included in
the Cancer Care Program (CCP).
Official Letters
1. Any request of any type of letters from GHD|EMPHNET employees should be
minimum 3 days prior to the needed date for the requested letter.
2. Employment letter is granted to the GHD|EMPHNET employees during the
contract period and based on a clear reason for the purpose of the letter.
3. Experience letter is granted to the GHD|EMPHNET employees after the end of the
contract if requested by the employees.
4. GHD|EMPHENT employees are eligible for a recommendation letter after
completing 1 year of service at GHD|EMPHNET.
5. Recommendation letter is only granted based on the Director approval.
6. Recommendation letter is granted to GHD|EMPHNE employees based on a clear
justification for the purpose of the letter.
